label: Bayside Property Management
text:
# Bayside Property Management

Our biggest commercial account: 62 rental units across the beachside zone. Contact is Marcus Lee, maintenance coordinator.

Contract: 20 guaranteed hours/month at $78/hour (see [[Pricing Guide]]), turnovers within 72 hours of move-out. Billing is monthly, net-15, through the [[Invoicing Workflow]].

Most work is the [[Bayside Turnover Punch List]]: patch, paint touch-up, fixtures, door hardware. They represent about 28% of revenue, which is a concentration risk flagged in the Monthly Cash Flow review.

Renewal is due in January. Marcus asked for a 5% discount on renewal; we'll counter with priority Monday scheduling instead.

label: Hendricks Family
text:
# Hendricks Family

Long-time residential client in the beachside zone. Tom and Linda Hendricks, retired, two dogs (keep the side gate closed).

History: ceiling fans 2024, gutter guards 2025, and the 2026 [[Hendricks Deck Repair]]. They referred two neighbors through the Referral Program last spring.

Preferences: call Linda, not Tom. Morning appointments only. They pay by check on completion and always tip the crew.

Next opportunity: they've asked about a screened porch quote for spring, likely over $2,500 so it needs a written quote per the [[Pricing Guide]].

label: Martinez Rental Portfolio
text:
# Martinez Rental Portfolio

Carlos Martinez owns 9 single-family rentals, three of them just over the county line — the only exception to our Service Area rule because he's been with us since year one.

Work is mostly repairs between tenants: drywall, doors, plumbing fixtures. See [[Martinez Drywall Patch]] for the most recent.

He pays by ACH within a week. He prefers photo updates by text at the start and end of each job. Carlos has hinted he may sell two units next year, which would reduce volume.

label: Oakview HOA
text:
# Oakview HOA

Homeowners association for the Oakview subdivision, 140 homes. Contact is the board treasurer, Priya Shah.

We handle common-area work: entry sign repairs, the clubhouse doors, pool fence, and the 2026 [[Oakview Fence Replacement]]. HOA pays net-30 and requires a certificate of insurance on file every year (see [[Insurance Policy]]).

Upside: individual homeowners in Oakview see our truck constantly, which drives residential leads. Roughly 1 in 5 Google Business Profile leads mention Oakview.

Board meets the second Tuesday of each month; quotes need to land by the Friday before.

label: Seaside Cafe
text:
# Seaside Cafe

Small restaurant downtown, owner Jenna Brooks. Commercial client, billed at standard rate.

Work so far: walk-in cooler door gasket, patio railing repair, and the [[Seaside Cafe Door Rehang]]. Work has to happen before 7 AM or after 3 PM when the kitchen is closed.

Jenna is active on social media and posted about us after the door job, which brought three leads. She'd be a good case study for the [[Website Redesign]].

label: Insurance Policy
text:
# Insurance Policy

General liability: $1M per occurrence / $2M aggregate, renews every March. Commercial auto on the truck. Workers' comp added when Dan Rivera was hired.

Certificates of insurance must be sent annually to [[Oakview HOA]] and Bayside Property Management before any work.

The insurer requires a documented [[Safety Checklist]] and monthly fire extinguisher checks. Premium for 2026: $4,860, paid quarterly — tracked in Monthly Cash Flow.

label: Invoicing Workflow
text:
# Invoicing Workflow

- Residential: invoice sent from the truck on completion; card, check, or ACH. Due on receipt.
- Jobs over $2,500: 30% deposit at booking, balance on completion (per the [[Pricing Guide]]).
- Commercial/HOA: monthly statement on the 1st; Bayside is net-15, Oakview HOA net-30.
- Reminders at 7 and 21 days past due; at 45 days, phone call from Kevin; at 60 days, work is paused.

Materials receipts from Coastal Lumber are attached to each invoice so markup is transparent. Reviewed weekly against the [[Monthly Cash Flow]].

label: Monthly Cash Flow
text:
# Monthly Cash Flow

Average monthly revenue 2026: $38,500. Labor (Dan Rivera + Kevin draw) is the largest cost, then materials, then truck costs.

Concentration risk: [[Bayside Property Management]] is 28% of revenue. Target is under 25% by growing residential through the Referral Program and Google Business Profile.

Seasonality: September peaks with Storm Prep Shutters; January is the slowest month, so we keep two months of expenses in reserve.

Receivables: HOA and commercial clients on net terms. Anything over 45 days goes to the collections step of the [[Invoicing Workflow]].

label: Truck Expenses
text:
# Truck Expenses

One work truck (2021 F-250) plus Dan Rivera's personal truck reimbursed at the IRS mileage rate.

2026 monthly averages: fuel $640, maintenance $120, insurance (part of the [[Insurance Policy]]) $210, mileage reimbursement $310.

Fuel spiked in June with the extended-zone jobs — another reason for the trip charge in the [[Service Area]] rules. Considering a second truck in 2027 if the Hiring Plan goes ahead.

label: Bayside Turnover Punch List
text:
# Bayside Turnover Punch List

Standard checklist for [[Bayside Property Management]] unit turnovers:
- Patch nail holes and touch-up paint (unit paint codes on file)
- Replace burned-out bulbs, check smoke detectors
- Tighten/replace door hardware and cabinet hinges
- Re-caulk tub and kitchen sink
- Test all GFCIs, faucets, and the garbage disposal
- Photos of every room before and after

Average turnover is 4.5 hours. Goal is to keep it under 5 so the 72-hour turnaround holds. Scheduled Mondays per the [[Scheduling Rules]].

label: Hendricks Deck Repair
text:
# Hendricks Deck Repair

Client: [[Hendricks Family]]. Completed April 2026.

Scope: replaced 14 rotted deck boards, 2 joists, and the stair stringers; sanded and stained with oil-based semi-transparent stain.

Materials from [[Coastal Lumber]]: pressure-treated 2x6 and 5/4 decking, $1,140 at cost. Labor: 22 hours across two days with Dan Rivera.

Total invoiced: $3,181 (labor $1,870, materials $1,311 with markup). 30% deposit collected up front because it was over $2,500. Lesson: stain needed 48 hours dry time, which pushed the job into a rain day — the Scheduling Rules now block two dry days for exterior stain jobs.

label: Martinez Drywall Patch
text:
# Martinez Drywall Patch

Client: [[Martinez Rental Portfolio]]. Completed September 2026.

Tenant moved out leaving a 3x4 ft hole behind a door plus a dozen anchor holes. Cut and patched, three coats of mud, sanded, primed, and painted.

Labor 7 hours across two visits (mud dry time). Materials from Coastal Lumber. Invoiced $742.

Dust got into the HVAC return, so the [[Safety Checklist]] now requires covering returns and wearing masks for all sanding.

label: Oakview Fence Replacement
text:
# Oakview Fence Replacement

Client: [[Oakview HOA]]. Completed June 2026.

Scope: removed 180 linear feet of failing wood pool fence and installed aluminum fence to meet pool code, plus two self-closing gates.

Fence panels ordered through [[Coastal Lumber]] with a 3-week lead time. Labor: 46 hours, two-person crew.

Invoiced $9,850, paid net-30 on time. One warranty callback for a sagging gate hinge (see [[Warranty Policy]]). Board was happy and asked us to quote the clubhouse deck next.

label: Seaside Cafe Door Rehang
text:
# Seaside Cafe Door Rehang

Client: [[Seaside Cafe]]. Completed August 2026.

The front entry door was dragging on the threshold after summer humidity. Rehung on new heavy-duty hinges, planed the bottom edge, sealed it, and adjusted the closer.

Billed at the flat $140 door rehang rate from the [[Pricing Guide]] plus $46 in hardware. Done at 6 AM before opening.

Jenna posted photos on social media the same day; three new leads came from it, which we're tracking in the Referral Program.

label: Storm Prep Shutters
text:
# Storm Prep Shutters

Seasonal job type. Each fall we install or inspect storm shutters for about 25 homeowners, mostly in the beachside zone and Oakview.

Pricing: $45 per opening to install, $25 per opening to inspect only. Average job is 12 openings.

Booked on Friday afternoons reserved for storm work per the [[Scheduling Rules]]. When a named storm is forecast, we text the shutter list and work existing clients first.

This job type is about 9% of annual revenue and a big part of September in the [[Monthly Cash Flow]].

label: Google Business Profile
text:
# Google Business Profile

Our top lead source: about 45% of new leads. 4.8 stars, 112 reviews.

Weekly routine: post one before/after photo, answer any Q&A, and reply to every review within 48 hours using the Review Responses templates.

Categories: Handyman, Carpenter, Fence Contractor. Service area matches the [[Service Area]] note.

Messages from the profile go straight into the [[Job Intake Process]]. Goal for 2026: 150 reviews by December.

label: Referral Program
text:
# Referral Program

Existing clients get $50 off their next job for each referred client who books. The referred client gets 10% off their first job — the maximum discount we allow under the [[Pricing Guide]].

Top referrers: the [[Hendricks Family]] (2 referrals) and Jenna at Seaside Cafe (3 leads from one post).

Referrals convert at 78%, far better than any paid channel. We track the source in the Job Intake Process and review results in the Monthly Cash Flow meeting.

label: Review Responses
text:
# Review Responses

Templates for replying to reviews on the [[Google Business Profile]].

5-star: Thank them by name, mention the specific job, and invite them back. Example: "Thanks, Linda! The deck came out great — enjoy it this summer."

3-star or below: Respond within 24 hours, apologize without arguing, offer a call, and schedule a free warranty visit if it's workmanship (see [[Warranty Policy]]).

Never mention prices or other clients by name in public replies.

label: Spring Promo
text:
# Spring Promo

March-April 2026 campaign: "Spring Fix-It List" — book 4+ hours of small jobs, get 10% off.

Results: 31 bookings, $14,200 in revenue, average ticket $458. Cost was about $600 in Google ads plus postcards to Oakview.

Discount stays at 10% max, never stacked with the [[Referral Program]].

Plan to repeat in 2027 with the [[Website Redesign]] landing page and earlier postcard timing (mid-February).

label: Website Redesign
text:
# Website Redesign

Current site is slow on mobile and has no online booking. Plan for Q1 2027:
- Online booking form that feeds the [[Job Intake Process]]
- Service pages for decks, fences, doors, drywall, and storm shutters
- Case studies: [[Hendricks Deck Repair]], Oakview Fence Replacement, Seaside Cafe Door Rehang
- Reviews widget pulled from Google Business Profile
- Spring Promo landing page

Budget $4,000. Get two quotes; decide by December based on the Monthly Cash Flow.

label: Job Intake Process
text:
# Job Intake Process

1. Lead comes in by phone, website form, or Google Business Profile message.
2. Within 1 business hour, call back and fill the intake sheet: address, scope, photos, access notes, pets.
3. Check the address against the Service Area note and quote the trip charge if needed.
4. If the job is under 4 hours, book directly using the [[Scheduling Rules]]. Over 4 hours, schedule a free 20-minute estimate visit.
5. Send confirmation text with arrival window and the [[Warranty Policy]] link.
6. Log the lead source so the Referral Program and Spring Promo can be tracked in Monthly Cash Flow reviews.

Target: 60% of estimates convert to booked jobs. Last quarter we hit 54%.

label: Pricing Guide
text:
# Pricing Guide

Our standard labor rate is $85/hour with a 2-hour minimum for residential calls. Commercial accounts like Bayside Property Management get a contracted rate of $78/hour in exchange for a guaranteed 20 hours a month.

Flat-rate items: TV mount $149, ceiling fan swap $175, door rehang $140, faucet replacement $160 (customer-supplied fixture). Materials are billed at cost plus 15%, pulled from [[Coastal Lumber]] where possible.

Trip charge of $35 applies outside the core zones defined in the Service Area note. Any job estimated over $2,500 needs a written quote and a 30% deposit per the [[Invoicing Workflow]]. Discounts are capped at 10% and only through the Referral Program or the Spring Promo.

label: Safety Checklist
text:
# Safety Checklist

Every job, before tools come out:
- Walk the site, note trip hazards, pets, and overhead lines.
- Ladder over 12 ft: second person on site, ladder tied off.
- Shut off breaker for any electrical work and test with the non-contact tester.
- Dust masks for drywall sanding (the Martinez Drywall Patch job taught us this the hard way).
- Respirator and ventilation for any oil-based stain, like the Hendricks Deck Repair.
- First aid kit and fire extinguisher checked monthly in the truck — tied to the [[Insurance Policy]] requirements.

Incidents get written up the same day and reviewed in the Monday meeting.

label: Scheduling Rules
text:
# Scheduling Rules

- Arrival windows are 2 hours, first job 8:00-10:00.
- No more than 3 residential jobs per tech per day; drive time eats the margin otherwise.
- Bayside Property Management turnovers get priority on Mondays because their tenants move out on weekends (see [[Bayside Turnover Punch List]]).
- Friday afternoons are held for storm and emergency calls June-November.
- Any job needing two people (decks, fences, heavy doors) is booked only on days Dan Rivera is on the schedule.
- Rain days: exterior work is rescheduled by 7:00 AM with a text to the client.

Follows the [[Safety Checklist]] for anything involving ladders over 12 feet.

label: Service Area
text:
# Service Area

Core zones (no trip charge): the beachside neighborhoods, downtown, and the Oakview subdivision. Extended zones (+$35 trip charge, see [[Pricing Guide]]): the inland ranch roads and anything more than 25 minutes from the shop.

We do not take jobs across the county line unless it's an existing client such as the Martinez Rental Portfolio. Dan Rivera covers the north routes on Tuesdays and Thursdays; Kevin takes the south side.

Storm season (June-November) we reserve Friday afternoons for emergency calls, per the [[Scheduling Rules]].

label: Warranty Policy
text:
# Warranty Policy

Workmanship is guaranteed for 12 months. Materials carry the manufacturer's warranty only.

Not covered: damage from storms, tenant abuse, or other contractors working on the same item. Customer-supplied parts are labor-only warranty for 90 days.

Warranty callbacks are scheduled within 5 business days and are never billed. We track callback rate monthly; anything above 3% of jobs triggers a review with Dan Rivera. The Oakview Fence Replacement had one callback for a sagging gate, fixed in 30 minutes.

Link is included in every confirmation text per the [[Job Intake Process]].

label: Coastal Lumber
text:
# Coastal Lumber

Primary supplier for lumber, decking, fence panels, and drywall. Contractor account with 8% off retail and net-30 terms.

Contact: Ray at the pro desk. Orders before 10 AM deliver the next day for free over $500.

Used on the [[Hendricks Deck Repair]] and the [[Oakview Fence Replacement]] (3-week lead time on aluminum panels). Receipts get attached per the [[Invoicing Workflow]].

Watch: prices on pressure-treated lumber went up 6% in August 2026; update the Pricing Guide estimates if it continues.

label: Dan Rivera
text:
# Dan Rivera

Lead technician, hired March 2025. 15 years of carpentry experience; best at decks, fences, and finish carpentry. Works Tuesday-Saturday.

Led the [[Hendricks Deck Repair]] and the [[Oakview Fence Replacement]]. Covers the north routes per the Service Area note.

Pay: $32/hour plus mileage (see Truck Expenses). Reviews are every March; he's asked about a path to crew lead if the [[Hiring Plan]] adds a second tech.

label: Hiring Plan
text:
# Hiring Plan

Goal: hire a second technician by spring 2027 so we can take more two-person jobs without blocking Dan Rivera's schedule.

Profile: 3+ years general repair, own tools, clean driving record, comfortable with drywall and plumbing fixtures (most Bayside turnover work).

Budget: $24-28/hour. Break-even requires roughly 25 more billable hours a month — likely from Bayside Property Management growth and residential leads.

New hires go through the [[Onboarding Checklist]]. Would require a second truck (see [[Truck Expenses]]).

label: Onboarding Checklist
text:
# Onboarding Checklist

Week 1:
- Paperwork: W-4, I-9, workers' comp enrollment per the [[Insurance Policy]]
- Ride-along with Dan Rivera for 3 days
- Review the [[Safety Checklist]] and sign off
- Learn the Bayside Turnover Punch List on a real unit

Week 2:
- Solo small jobs (under 2 hours) with photo check-ins
- Learn the Job Intake Process and how to quote flat-rate items from the Pricing Guide

30-day review with Kevin.
